# Mistral is launching a 1-trillion-parameter open AI model it claims leads outside China

The French startup says ML4, trained on 4,000 Nvidia GPUs in Europe, leads open-weight models outside China by a substantial margin

By Cris Tolomia·2 min read·Updated October 6, 2026

Add QZ to Google

NurPhoto / Getty Images

Mistral AI introduced a new open-weight AI model on Tuesday, claiming it outperforms every rival built outside China at a moment when Western developers are working to match the progress of their Chinese counterparts. [...] The model was trained from scratch on 4,000 Nvidia$NVDA Grace Blackwell GPUs over two months inside Mistral's own European data centers. It covers more than 160 languages, including every official E.U. language, the company said.

Mistral is pitching ML4 on its cybersecurity capabilities in particular, arguing that open-weight models give enterprises and governments a way to defend against threat actors who exploit closed systems. "The cyber defence capabilities will enable enterprises and governments to defend themselves against threat actors that are jailbreaking closed models to perform cyber attacks," said Guillaume Lample, co-founder and chief scientist of Mistral, in a statement.

results.title: Mistral’s new 1T model aims to leapfrog closed and open rivals | TechCrunch
results.content:
The race between open and closed AI is on, and Europe is still in the mix. On Tuesday, French AI lab Mistral AI has released Mistral Large 4, a new large multimodal model aiming to leapfrog both American and Chinese rivals — following what French president Macron has described as “a third way in AI.”

Amid a growing divide between closed models that can be unplugged and open models that are often made in China, Mistral is positioning ML4 as an alternative to both. Nicknamed Le Chonk in reference to its one trillion parameters, ML4 is definitely not small; but is not an open-weight model yet. For the time being, it can only be accessed via a public guardrail endpoint, but Mistral plans to make its weights available in just three weeks, after safety testing is complete.

It says the model beats some closed frontier models at visual grounding, meaning it can accurately identify and locate specific objects or areas inside an image.  
  
The model was developed entirely in Europe and is available through Mistral’s API.

Mistral has unveiled Mistral Large 4, or "le Chonk," a 1-trillion-parameter model that it says is the strongest open-weight AI model developed outside China by a wide margin. The model is entering preview for developers, cybersecurity teams and governments before a broader release later this month. CNBC reports: ML4 was trained on 4,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs over two months that were deployed in Mistral's own data centers in Europe. When its core parameters are released, ML4 will rank among the top open-weight models globally on aggregate benchmark performance, Mistral said in a statement. The company added that ML4 was the strongest open-weight model developed outside China by a "substantial margin." The new model still lags behind the frontier in areas such as coding.

# Mistral Large 4

By Mistral AI

Model family: Mistral

Mistral Large 4 is an open-weight, general-purpose multimodal model built on a granular Mixture-of-Experts design with 1.05T total and 49B active parameters, plus a 1.6B vision encoder. It takes text and image input and returns text, with a 1M token context window. Supported features include function calling, structured outputs, document question answering, prefix completion, batch processing, and built-in tools for agents and conversations. It is aimed at demanding workloads such as software engineering, cyber defense, manufacturing, finance, and visual grounding, and is trained across 160+ languages. Currently available through the API as a public preview, with open weights planned for the end of October 2026.

## Overview

Mistral Large 4 is a general-purpose multimodal model with a granular Mixture-of-Experts architecture. It has 1.05T total parameters with 49B active per token and a 1.6B vision encoder. It accepts text and image input, produces text output, and supports a 1M token context window. Released as a public preview on the API, with open weights planned for release at the end of October 2026.
